title: Natural Failures and Subtask-Guided Recovery in RoboCasa
Executive summary
source_paragraphs: Use RoboCasa as the primary benchmark, retain pi0 as a weak-policy baseline, and add RLDX-1 as the higher-progress policy. The most defensible first contribution is not a fully retrained recovery VLA. It is a modular system that detects failure early, returns the end effector to a last-good anchor, and chooses among policy-generated action chunks with a subtask-conditioned critic.

Recovery demonstrations are not required for locally retryable failures when the environment remains task-valid and the base policy assigns some probability to a successful continuation. They become necessary for state-breaking failures, unsafe rollback motion, or repeated proposal-support failure.

The dataset should remain centered on natural on-policy failures, with expert-derived perturbations used as controlled augmentation rather than as the main scientific claim. The project becomes stronger if it measures how recovery changes across policy competence levels instead of treating one policy's failure distribution as universal.

implications: Integrate the released RLDX-1 RoboCasa checkpoint behind the existing model-agnostic policy interface.
Run a six-task pilot with matched pi0 and RLDX-1 rollouts; estimate useful-failure yield and failure-depth distributions before recollecting at scale.
Extend annotations with failure onset, last-good checkpoint, retryable/state-breaking class, completed prefix, and forked candidate outcomes.
Implement EEF rollback plus unguided retry as the minimum baseline.
Train the subtask critic and compare reranking against unguided retry from identical checkpoints.
Add the learned monitor only after the oracle-onset recovery experiment works.
Attempt direct flow guidance only after reranking demonstrates that successful policy proposals exist at the recovered states.
Collect explicit reset trajectories only for the residual state-breaking failure set.

title: Limitations and robustness checks
source_paragraphs: Simulator privilege: EEF pose restoration must be reported separately from full environment restoration; the latter is an oracle.
Policy dependence: failure distributions shift with policy competence. Train/evaluate across pi0 and RLDX-1, or explicitly limit claims to one policy family.
Multiple valid subtask orders: condition on semantic subtask identity and the observed completed prefix, not a fixed global index.
Success is not safety: add drop, contact, spill, collision, and success-but-unsafe metrics rather than relying only on task predicates.
Critic exploitation: compare critic predictions with deterministic fork outcomes, monitor calibration, and test whether aggressive guidance degrades clean rollouts.
Benchmark validity: use paired seeds, confidence intervals, and shortcut/leakage checks; RoboCasa performs comparatively well in recent audits but is not immune to benchmark artifacts.
